seoTitle: Free Prometheus Alert Rule Generator Online
metaDescription: Generate a Prometheus alerting rules file with ready-made alerts for downtime, CPU, memory, disk, 5xx errors, latency, crash loops and certificates.
intro: List the alerts you want, with optional thresholds, and get a Prometheus rules file with PromQL expressions, severity labels and summaries.
why:
Almost every Prometheus setup ends up with the same first alerts: a target that is down, a busy CPU, a full disk, a spike in 5xx responses. The PromQL for each is easy to get slightly wrong, for example a disk query that counts tmpfs or a CPU expression that forgets to average by instance.

This generator holds eight tested-looking patterns and writes them into a rules group with your chosen for: duration and an optional team label. Metric names assume node_exporter, kube-state-metrics, blackbox exporter and a typical http_requests_total counter, so adjust them to what your services export. Use promtool check rules before loading the file.
howTo: Enter one alert per line, with an optional threshold, such as HighCpu 85.
Set the group name, the for: duration and, if you like, a team label.
Save the output as a rules file, run promtool check rules, then reference it in rule_files.

faq.a: InstanceDown, HighCpu, HighMemory, DiskLow, High5xxRate, HighLatencyP95, PodCrashLooping and CertExpiry. An unknown name stops with an error listing these.
Each alert has its own default: percent for CPU, memory, disk and 5xx, seconds for latency, restarts for crash loops and days for certificate expiry. The number you type replaces that default.

faq.q: Will the metrics exist in my setup?
faq.a: Only if you run the matching exporters. The expressions use node_exporter, kube-state-metrics, blackbox and http_requests_total names. Rename metrics to match your own instrumentation.
No. It only fills in the templates. Run promtool check rules on the file to catch syntax problems.
